intro: The octagonal G-Shock with a polished steel bezel.
why: The GM-2100-1A wraps the octagonal shape in a forged and molded stainless steel bezel with a polished finish. It keeps the 200 m water resistance and shock resistance, adds a double LED light and world time, and weighs 72 g.
tradeoff: It runs on batteries (about 3 years), with no solar charging or Bluetooth, and the steel bezel makes it heavier than the resin GA-2100.
facts: 49.3 x 44.4 x 11.8 mm, 72 g, stainless steel bezel

name: Noah x Timex Boatswain
alt: Noah x Timex Boatswain TW6A31200, manufacturer product view
label: For an oval Noah collaboration
intro: A cream Roman-numeral dial with a rope motif.
why: The Boatswain is a Noah collaboration with Timex, and the cream dial carries black Roman numerals and an oval rope motif. The 31 mm silver-tone steel case sits on a brown pebbled leather strap, and the Noah logo is engraved on the caseback.
tradeoff: It's a quartz dress watch, and the 30 m rating covers hand-washing and splashes only. Timex says it isn't suitable for swimming or diving. This guide covers the silver-tone TW6A31200; the gold-tone version is TW6A31100, so check the reference before ordering.
facts: 31 mm polished stainless steel case, 7 mm thick
Brown leather strap, 30 m water resistance (splashes only)
